analysis.title: Sunrun Inc. (RUN): Near-term cash generation reset somewhat expected on weaker macro, but growth set to turn more positive into 2027; Buy
key_insights: RUN reported mixed 3Q26 results: revenue $1.10bn (+52% yoy) beat GSe $880mn and FactSet consensus $758mn, but solar installations and subscriber additions fell yoy.
3Q26 subscriber additions were ~23k (-24% yoy). Solar installations were ~204MW (-15% yoy) vs GSe 227MW. Storage installed was ~374MWh (-9% yoy) vs GSe ~404MWh.
Revenue was supported by the non-retained or partially retained model. Energy Systems and Product Sales revenue rose ~134% yoy to ~$546mn.
Direct installations returned to growth at +9% yoy after the company rebuilt its direct sales organization. Storage attach rate hit a record 75%.

FY26 cash generation guidance was cut to ~$200mn excluding equipment safe harbor investments, the low end of the prior $200mn-$375mn range. Aggregate subscriber value is now ~$4.6bn, the low end of the prior $4.6bn-$4.9bn.

Management attributed the cash generation cut mainly to lower volume expectations, with higher interest rates a secondary factor. 3Q26 cash generation was ~$56mn excluding ~$50mn of safe harbor investments, or ~$6mn including them. Management expects higher cash generation in 4Q26.
Upfront net subscriber value rose to ~$3,718/subscriber in 3Q26 from ~$2,016 in 2Q26. Margin expanded to 7.1% from 3.7% even though the project-level discount rate rose to 8.4% from 7.3%.

Direct sales grew high-single to low-double digits yoy each month from June through October. The affiliate channel remained down 67% yoy. Management expects overall installations to grow yoy in 2027, with all routes including affiliate possibly growing by ~2Q27. Illinois, Texas and New Jersey are growing >25% yoy.

Networked storage capacity passed ~5.0GWh, and management expects it to double by YE28. Distributed power plants are expected to add to cash generation in 2027, with the PG&E/Google transaction cited as an early proof point for the Tesla Renew consortium.

GS raised its 12-month price target to $13 from $11 on a NAV valuation. 2027 assets carry $11/sh unchanged, and a 1.0X multiple (from 0.0X) is applied to $2/sh (from $0/sh) of future NAV creation. Rating stays Buy, with 47.9% upside from $8.79.

GS cut 2026E-2028E MW estimates to 738/804/868MW from 774/844/911MW. Revenue estimates are now $3,447mn/$3,419mn/$3,803mn vs prior $3,241mn/$3,517mn/$3,917mn. GAAP diluted EPS is now $1.35/$0.26/$1.18 vs prior $0.69/($0.05)/$0.88.
Key risks named are slower MW growth, net metering policy shifts, and higher interest rates.

market_movers.rationale: Direct installs returned to growth, storage attach hit a record 75%, and upfront net subscriber value margin improved, supporting a better 2027 setup despite the FY26 cash generation cut. Price target raised to $13 from $11.

sector_views.rationale: The report covers RUN only. Near-term volume and cash generation are pressured, while direct channel growth and storage monetization are offsets.

3Q26 EBITDA $350.1mn reported vs GSe $217.6mn estimate. Operating income $153.5mn reported vs GSe $18.7mn estimate.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The observed discount rate rose from 7.3% in 2Q26, a headwind to subscriber value, though upfront net subscriber value margin still improved.

risk_factors: Lower volume expectations drove the FY26 cash generation reduction.
Net debt/EBITDA of 13.0x in 2025E and net debt/equity above 250% through 2028E.
